cells.tense: Right now you're steering from something you actually saw, and the choosing has your hand on it.
cells.ask: Give one steady hour to the thing this clearing made room for — let the practice, not the flash, hold the gain
cells.core:
You walk in, you see what's flimsy, and you say so — to the plan, to the room, to yourself — and then you pick the next thing and mean it. No drama in the decision, no forcing it. The direction stands because it's resting on ground that's actually there, and the people around you can feel that it'll hold.

What keeps it standing isn't the next insight. It's the same work, done again, quietly, on a schedule that doesn't care whether you feel inspired. Pick one thing this clearing opened up and give it regular, unhurried attention. That's how a moment of seeing turns into something you can live on.
cells.sheetLine: You saw what couldn't hold and chose past it — now let steady practice keep it.
cells.verb: letting what can't stand fall away
cells.place: standing at the point where a direction gets chosen

cells.tense: You're braced for the next collapse before it's here — standing in a future where everything's already coming down.
cells.ask: Take one thing you're tearing down and pass it to someone who keeps it alive — let it travel through other hands before you finish the job
cells.core:
You're not waiting for things to fall — you're going ahead and knocking them loose, calling it freedom. Every solid thing gets tested until it cracks, and nothing gets to stand long enough to be useful. The clearing you used to receive, you're now manufacturing, and the direction you were supposed to pick has gone missing in it.

When this is steady, you can take what's built and hand it to someone without inspecting it to death first. Try that with one thing today: give it to someone who'll carry it, change it, teach it their way. Meaning survives by being passed along, not by being audited. The direction that returns is one more than one person is holding up — and that's a thing that stands.
cells.sheetLine: You're knocking things down faster than insight can clear them.

cells.tense: You're still standing at a door that already closed, holding up a frame with nothing left in it.
cells.ask: Build one small structure today — a fixed time, a written rule, a place where the thing you're trying to hold gets organized
cells.core:
Something's already gone and you're still propping it up — the schedule, the plan, the version of this that stopped being true. Holding it costs you the direction you'd rather be choosing.

Working well, you walk into a room and things make sense — you can put chaos into a shape people can move through, and it holds because it serves what it's holding. Set one clear container today: a time, a rule, a line you keep. Structure like that isn't a cage; it's what makes the next choice possible. Give it one place to stand and the current comes back into your hands.
cells.sheetLine: You're holding up a structure that's already stopped holding.

cells.tense: The pen is down, but you're writing — you're steering this and calling it something that's just happening to you.
cells.ask: Notice one thing you're already pushing toward and name the wanting underneath it — let the direction come from that, not from the next clearing
cells.core:
Something in you is already choosing — the way you lean, what you keep doing, the direction you keep drifting — and you're talking about it like the situation is doing the choosing. Some of what's standing around you is about to fall, and it's falling because of a push you haven't owned yet.

On a good day, this has a feeling running through it. You move because something matters, not because another wall came down, and the wanting is what's driving. Before the next break, put your hand on one thing you're already moving toward and say out loud what you actually want there. The clearing doesn't decide your life; the wanting does, once you let it drive.
cells.sheetLine: You're already steering this — you haven't said the wanting that's doing it.
